newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks shrug Dow to inch up at close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks shrug Dow to inch up at close.

text.p: Mexican stocks withstood plunging share prices and ended ahead for the first time in three sessions on Friday after wavering through the day on cautious trade ahead of key economic dataes next week, traders and analysts said.
"We're waiting for news like GDP here and the outcome of next week's FOMC meeting," said Hector Jimenez, an analyst at the Inverlat brokerage.
The leading IPC share index ended up 3.16 points, or 0.08 percent, at 3,890.36. Trading volume was lackluster at 73.6 million shares.
"Volume was not bad, but you could see caution in there. Next week's data will be crucial for deciding whether to step into the market, or not," Jimenez said.

Mexico's Finance Ministry is expected to announce first quarter GDP on Monday, May 19. Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz told journalists on Thursday he expected GDP to grow by 4.5-5.0 percent. This compares with growth of 5.12 percent forecast on average in a Reuters survey. The Federal Open Market Committee will meet on May 20 to determine U.S. interest rate policy.
Traders said selective buying helped bolster the market and resist the slide on the Dow Jones, which dropped 138.88 points to 7,194.67.
"When the Dow began to slide, we followed suit, but pushing and shoving at the close was due to selective buying that propped it up," a desk trader said.
The IPC rose as high as 3,901.51 points, or 14.31 points ahead, in early trade on what dealers said was a delayed reaction to public finance data released on Thursday.
Financial stock Bancomer contributed most to propping up the market, gaining three centavos to 2.94 pesos.
Bancomer, which accounted for 17 percent of all shares traded, is a creditor of the troubled conglomerate Grupo Sidek, for which some traders expected a debt restructuring deal to be announced soon.
Telmex, usually the most traded stock on the bourse, weighed most on trading after Bancomer and accounted for 16 percent of all shares traded.
The telecomms stock ended off two centavos at 17.12 pesos, while its ADRs declined 1/4 to 43-3/8.
Traders also drew attention to retail stock Soriana, up 1.20 pesos to 19.00 pesos in brisk trade.
Dealers said interest in the stock, which made an infrequent appearance on the most-traded stocks list, was enhanced by a long-term buy recommendation issued by the Serfin financial group.
On the broad market, 106 stocks changed hands, of which gainers outnumbered sliders by 50 to 38.
Analysts said the bourse could begin to rally once uncertainy over next week's data had receded.
"I don't rule out new records at the end of next week," Jimenez said.
